newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan chip makers raise 16 megabit DRAM chip prices.
newsitem.headline: Japan chip makers raise 16 megabit DRAM chip prices.

text.p: Japanese computer chip makers raised their prices in February, following the recent recovery in spot prices worldwide, company officials said Monday.
They said the price hike for memory chips should help improve their businesses, hit hard by a tumble in chip prices last year.

NEC Corp. and Toshiba Corp. said they implemented a 5 percent to 10 percent hike in their prices of 16 megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips last month for some volume-users whose previous deals were made at relatively cheap levels.

"The price hike is due to a rise in the spot market, because Korean chip makers are reducing production," an NEC spokesman said. He said that chip prices in volume-user contracts were 800-900 yen ($6-$7) in February.
Spot prices for 16 megabit DRAM chips -- the current mainstay products used in PCs -- have gone up to around $9 from around $6 earlier this year, he said.

Steven Appleton, president of U.S. chip maker Micron Technology Inc., also said last week in San Francisco that spot prices for 16-megabit DRAM chips have risen about 50 percent since Korean suppliers revealed plans to limit output.
In late January, South Korea's Samsung Electronics Co., the world's largest producer of 16-megabit DRAMs, said that it would further control output of the chips.

Appleton said spot prices for DRAMs were currently about $9 to $9.50, adding that he expected further growth in the DRAM market as customers switch to more memory-intensive Microsoft Windows NT and Intel Pentium MMX multimedia processors.
